{{Short description|none}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2025}}
{{Use American English|date=November 2025}}
The knockout stage<!--- Do not bold per MOS:TITLEABSENTBOLD. See other world cups pages. ---> of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] was the second and final stage of the competition, following the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Group stage|group stage]]. Played from June 28 to July 19, 2026, the knockout stage ended with the [[2026 FIFA World Cup final|final]], held at [[MetLife Stadium]] in [[East Rutherford, New Jersey|East Rutherford]], [[New Jersey]].<ref name="match schedule">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 26 – Match Schedule |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=February 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260718135631/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |archive-date=18 July 2026}}</ref> The top two teams from each of the twelve groups, along with the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|best eight third-place teams]], advanced to the knockout stage to compete in a [[single-elimination tournament]]. There were 32 matches in the knockout stage, including a match for third place.<ref name="regulations">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 Regulations |publisher=FIFA |date=May 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623212158/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Format==
The knockout stage of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] was contested between 32 teams that qualify from the group stage. Matches in the knockout stage were played to a finish. If the score of a match was level at the end of 90 minutes of playing time, 30 minutes of [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] were played. If the scores were still tied, a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] determined the team that prevailed.<ref name="regulations"/> All times listed are local.<ref name="match schedule"/>

In the round of 32, four of the group winners played group runners-up. The other eight group winners played advancing third-place teams. The eight remaining group runners-up played against each other.

FIFA set out the following schedule for the round of 32:<ref name="regulations" />
*'''Match 73''': Runner-up Group A vs Runner-up Group B
*'''Match 74''': Winner Group E vs Third-place Group A/B/C/D/F
*'''Match 75''': Winner Group F vs Runner-up Group C
*'''Match 76''': Winner Group C vs Runner-up Group F
*'''Match 77''': Winner Group I vs Third-place Group C/D/F/G/H
*'''Match 78''': Runner-up Group E vs Runner-up Group I
*'''Match 79''': Winner Group A vs Third-place Group C/E/F/H/I
*'''Match 80''': Winner Group L vs Third-place Group E/H/I/J/K
*'''Match 81''': Winner Group D vs Third-place Group B/E/F/I/J
*'''Match 82''': Winner Group G vs Third-place Group A/E/H/I/J
*'''Match 83''': Runner-up Group K vs Runner-up Group L
*'''Match 84''': Winner Group H vs Runner-up Group J
*'''Match 85''': Winner Group B vs Third-place Group E/F/G/I/J
*'''Match 86''': Winner Group J vs Runner-up Group H
*'''Match 87''': Winner Group K vs Third-place Group D/E/I/J/L
*'''Match 88''': Runner-up Group D vs Runner-up Group G

===Combinations of matches in the round of 32===
The specific matchups involving the third-place teams depended on which eight third-place teams qualified for the round of 32. The 495 possible combinations were published in Annex C of the tournament regulations.<ref name="regulations"/>

The following eight groups had their third-place teams finish in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|top eight of the ranking]]: B, D, E, F, I, J, K, and L. According to the combinations table (outcome #67), the matchups involving third-place teams were therefore as follows:<ref name="regulations"/>
*1A (Mexico) vs 3E (Ecuador)
*1B (Switzerland) vs 3J (Algeria)
*1D (United States) vs 3B (Bosnia and Herzegovina)
*1E (Germany) vs 3D (Paraguay)
*1G (Belgium) vs 3I (Senegal)
*1I (France) vs 3F (Sweden)
*1K (Colombia) vs 3L (Ghana)
*1L (England) vs 3K (DR Congo)

==Round of 16==

===Canada vs Morocco===
The teams had faced each other four times previously, with Morocco being unbeaten in any of these matches. Their most recent match was in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup Group F#Canada vs Morocco|group stage of the previous World Cup]], which Morocco won 2–1.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/canada/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Morocco/|title=Canada national football team: record v Morocco|website=11v11.com|access-date=June 29, 2026}}</ref>

A [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Independence Day ceremonies|special ceremony]] commemorating the [[United States Semiquincentennial]], marking the 250th anniversary of the [[United States Declaration of Independence]], was held on the stadium grounds 25 minutes before kickoff.<ref name="FIFA250">{{Cite web |title=Pre-match US Independence Day celebrations to add to FIFA World Cup 2026™ action |url=https://inside.fifa.com/organisation/news/pre-match-us-independence-day-celebrations-world-cup-2026 |access-date=5 July 2026 |website=[[FIFA]]}}</ref>

In the 50th minute, Morocco took the lead when [[Azzedine Ounahi]] received the ball after a free-kick was cut-back to him from the right by [[Achraf Hakimi]], before he shot from the edge of the penalty area, low into the bottom right corner of the net.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx2jw3e9gq0t?page=2|title= Canada 0 Morocco 3|date=4 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>
Ounahi got a second goal in the 82nd minute with a finish from twelve yards out high to the top right corner of the net after a pass from [[Brahim Díaz]] from the right. 
[[Soufiane Rahimi]] made it 3–0 in the 98th minute with a low finish under the goalkeeper to the right corner of the net from the left of the penalty area after another pass from Díaz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/canada-vs-morocco/549854|title= World Cup 2026: Canada 0–3 Morocco – Azzedine Ounahi double helps knock out co-hosts to give 2022 semi-finalists last-eight spot|date=4 July 2026|work=Sky Sports|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>

With this result and Egypt's loss to Argentina, Morocco was the only African team to proceed to the quarterfinals while co-host Canada was eliminated, marking its best finish since its group-stage exits in 1986 and 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/world-cup-2026/2026/0704/1581749-moroccos-second-half-blitz-ends-canada-journey/|title= Morocco's second-half blitz ends Canada journey|date=4 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>

===Paraguay vs France===
[[File:Kylian Mbappe Diego Gomez France v Paraguay 4 July 2026-146.jpg|thumb|right|During the match between Paraguay and France.]]
Paraguay had never defeated France in their five previous encounters, including two matches at the FIFA World Cup: a [[1958 FIFA World Cup Group 2#France vs Paraguay|7–3 group stage loss]] in [[1958 FIFA World Cup|1958]] and a [[1998 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#France vs Paraguay|1–0 round of 16 defeat]] via [[golden goal]] at the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] (which France hosted and current manager [[Didier Deschamps]] also played in). Their latest meeting was a 5–0 friendly in 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/paraguay/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/France/|title=Paraguay national football team: record v France|website=11v11.com|access-date=June 29, 2026}}</ref>

The match was played in extreme heat, with temperatures up to {{cvt|38|C|F}} at kickoff time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cdx7jwdy5ndt|title=Paraguay 0 France 1|date=6 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>
In the 70th minute, France was awarded a penalty after a VAR intervention when substitute [[Désiré Doué]] was fouled inside the box by [[Diego Gómez (Paraguayan footballer)|Diego Gómez]]. [[Kylian Mbappé]] scored a penalty with a low shot to the right corner, sending Paraguay goalkeeper [[Orlando Gill]] the wrong way.
Paraguay committed 13 fouls to France's 11 during the game, but escaped without a single yellow card while France received three.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/05/paraguay-france-last-16-world-cup-match-report|title= Mbappé and France ditch 'tuxedos' to play 'dirty football' and beat Paraguay|date=6 July 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref> Global media were almost unanimous in condemning the Paraguayan team's systematic foul play,<ref>[https://www.rfi.fr/fr/sports/20260706-football-dégoûtant-totalement-honteux-la-presse-internationale-étrille-le-paraguay-après-son-match-face-à-la-france "«Football dégoûtant», «totalement honteux»: la presse internationale étrille le Paraguay après son match face à la France"], [[Radio France internationale]], 6 July 2026</ref> as well as [[Ilgiz Tantashev]]'s poor refereeing.<ref>[https://www.franceinfo.fr/coupe-du-monde/je-n-avais-jamais-joue-un-match-comme-ca-avec-autant-de-coups-l-arbitrage-de-france-paraguay-au-centre-des-debats-a-la-coupe-du-monde-2026_8095031.html ""Je n'avais jamais joué un match avec autant de coups, de coups en traître" : l'arbitrage de France-Paraguay au centre des débats à la Coupe du monde"], [[France Info]], 5 July 2026</ref>
 
Alongside the Canada vs Morocco match in Houston, a special ceremony commemorating the 250th anniversary of the United States Declaration of Independence was held on the stadium grounds 25 minutes before kickoff.<ref name="FIFA250" />

After the match, Paraguayan Senator, [[Celeste Amarilla]], racially abused Mbappé on social media and the latter made a statement on X in response. Amarilla made a response which was not well received.<ref name="AmarillaGuardian2026">{{cite news |title='A despicable woman': Kylian Mbappé hits out at Paraguayan senator over racist attack |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/06/a-despicable-women-kylian-mbappe-hits-out-at-paraguayan-senator-over-racist-attack |work=[[The Guardian]] |agency=[[Reuters]] |date=6 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="Geiger2026">{{cite news |last1=Geiger |first1=Chris |title=«Noix de coco», «chimpanzé»: une sénatrice se lâche contre Mbappé |url=https://www.20min.ch/fr/story/coupe-du-monde-2026-noix-de-coco-chimpanze-une-senatrice-se-lache-contre-mbappe-103597633 |access-date=6 July 2026 |work=[[20 minutes (France)|20 minutes]] |date=6 July 2026 |language=fr}}</ref><ref name="Peter2026">{{cite news |last=Peter |first=Mike |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ckg557wxrzro |title=Mbappe condemns racist posts from Paraguay senator |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=6 July 2026 }}</ref>

===Brazil vs Norway===
The teams had met four times previously, including once in the World Cup, a [[1998 FIFA World Cup Group A#Brazil vs Norway|2–1 group stage victory]] for Norway in [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]], and most recently in 2006, a 1–1 draw in a friendly to keep Norway's unbeaten head-to-head record. Norway is the only [[Brazil national football team records and statistics#Head-to-head record|team that Brazil has played]] but never defeated.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/brazil/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Norway/|title=Brazil national football team: record v Norway|website=11v11.com|access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref>

In the 15th minute, Brazil was awarded a penalty when [[Kristoffer Ajer]] fouled [[Matheus Cunha]] with a sliding tackle. [[Bruno Guimarães]]'s penalty to the right was saved by [[Ørjan Nyland]] after a stuttering run-up.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/05/brazil-norway-world-cup-2026-last-16-match-report|title= Haaland’s heroic double stuns Brazil and sends Norway into World Cup quarter-finals|date=5 July 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=13 October 2026}}</ref>

In the 79th minute, [[Erling Haaland]] gave Norway the lead when he headed into the right corner of the net from six yards out after a cross by [[Andreas Schjelderup]] from the left. In the 90th minute, Haaland scored again with a left foot shot from just outside the penalty area low to the right corner of the net. Brazil was awarded a penalty in the 10th minute of added time when [[Leo Ostigard]] elbowed [[Casemiro]]. [[Neymar]] scored low to the right of the net.
Norway held on to win 2–1 and advanced to the quarterfinals for the first time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c3wyl9qe4xgt|title= Brazil 1 Norway 2|date=5 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=13 October 2026}}</ref>

Brazil's loss marked the first time the team was eliminated in the round of 16 since the [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]] edition, when it lost to [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] [[1990 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Brazil vs Argentina|1–0]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49279982/brazil-norway-world-cup-2026-erling-haaland|title=Haaland, Norway condemn Brazil to earliest World Cup exit since 1990|website=ESPN.com|access-date= July 5, 2026}}</ref> This was Neymar's last match for Brazil; following the defeat, he announced his international retirement.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/neymar-confirms-brazil-retirement-world-232600653.html |title=Neymar confirms Brazil retirement after World Cup exit |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |date=6 July 2026 }}</ref>

===Mexico vs England===
[[File:Mexico v England (2026 FIFA World Cup - Round of 16).jpg|thumb|Pre-match ceremony between Mexico and England]]
The teams had previously faced each other nine times, most recently in 2010, a 3–1 win for England in a friendly match. They also met at the [[1966 FIFA World Cup]], when England, as the host, [[1966 FIFA World Cup Group 1#England vs Mexico|won 2–0]] in the group stage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/mexico/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/england/|title=Mexico national football team: record v England|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 1, 2026}}</ref> Additionally, they encountered each other at [[Estadio Azteca]] in a friendly that ended with a [[1985 Azteca 2000 Tournament|1–0 victory for Mexico in 1985]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/mexico-v-england-09-june-1985-239281/|title=Mexico v England, 9 June 1985|website=11v11.com|access-date= July 1, 2026}}</ref> This was also the first time that England had played at Estadio Azteca since its infamous [[Argentina v England (1986 FIFA World Cup)|match against Argentina in the 1986 World Cup]], in which England famously conceded Maradona's [[The hand of God|"hand of God" goal]] and the "[[Goal of the Century]]".

Before the match, it was reported that the game would be moved up to noon due to reports of inclement weather and lightning. However, after protests from both Mexico and England, FIFA reversed the decision and kept the kickoff at the original time.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mokbel |first1=Sami |last2=Kearns |first2=Sean |title=England-Mexico kick-off unchanged after Fifa U-turn |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvgmz3jyq9qo |publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=3 July 2026 |access-date=3 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ogden |first1=Mark |title=Sources: Mexico vs. England World Cup kickoff time unchanged after talks |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49260497/mexico-vs-england-world-cup-clash-brought-forward-six-hours-sources |publisher=[[ESPN FC]] |access-date=3 July 2026|date=3 July 2026}}</ref> An hour before the kickoff, FIFA delayed the match by one hour due to the aforementioned inclement weather.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pitt-Brooke |first1=Jack |title=England's World Cup clash with Mexico delayed due to bad weather: Live updates |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/mexico-vs-england-live-updates-world-cup-2026-score-result/1kXwPh7t8O2X/ |publisher=The New York Times |access-date=5 July 2026|date=5 July 2026}}</ref>

In the 36th minute, [[Jude Bellingham]] scored to put England into the lead with a diving header to the left of the net from just inside the six yard box after a cross from [[Bukayo Saka]] from the right. 98 seconds later it was 2–0 when Bellingham scored again with a low side-foot finish from just inside the six yard after a low cross from [[Harry Kane]] from the right. In the 42nd minute, [[Julián Quiñones]] pulled a goal back when he shot high to the net from eight yards out after the ball broke to him after a free kick from the left.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/england-mexico-world-cup-2026-result-highlights-goals-b3009452.html|title= England win World up thriller in Mexico to reveal true identity|date=6 July 2026|work=The Independent|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>

In the 54th minute, [[Jarell Quansah]] was sent off when he dived in with a high challenge on [[Jesús Gallardo]]. England was awarded a penalty in the 60th minute when [[Anthony Gordon (footballer)|Anthony Gordon]] was brought down by the diving Mexican goalkeeper [[Raúl Rangel (footballer)|Raúl Rangel]]. Kane scored the penalty with a shot to the left of the net to restore England's two-goal lead.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jul/05/mexico-v-england-world-cup-2026-last-16-live|title= Mexico 2 England 3: Live Updates|date=6 July 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>
In the 69th minute, Mexico was awarded a penalty when Kane kicked the foot of [[Brian Gutiérrez]] in the penalty area. [[Raúl Jiménez]] scored with a shot to the left corner, but Mexico was unable to find an equalizer, with 11 minutes added on at the end.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr5j14eyzm8t|title= Mexico 2 England 3|date=6 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>

This match marked the first time Mexico lost a World Cup game at the Azteca, and only the third time it lost a competitive game at the Azteca in its entire history.<ref>{{Cite web |website=ABC News| last=Smale |first=Simon |date=6 July 2026 |title=World Cup updates: England stuns Mexico in thriller at the Azteca, Brazil 0-2 Norway in New Jersey |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-07-06/world-cup-live-brazil-vs-norway-mexico-vs-england/106881396 |access-date=13 October 2026}}</ref> The defeat also made Mexico the second co-host to be eliminated after Canada, and marked the first time Mexico hosted the tournament without reaching the quarterfinals, failing to match its runs in the [[1970 FIFA World Cup|1970]] and [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]] editions of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.thenationalherald.com/england-hands-mexico-its-first-world-cup-loss-at-estadio-azteca-winning-3-2-to-reach-quarterfinals/|title=England hands Mexico its first World Cup loss at Estadio Azteca, winning 3–2 to reach quarterfinals|website=[[The National Herald]]|access-date= July 6, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49283101/england-end-mexico-world-cup-best-win-foreign-soil-their-history
|title=England end Mexico's World Cup with best win on foreign soil in their history|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date= July 5, 2026}}</ref>

This was the final match played in Mexico for the remainder of the tournament.

===Portugal vs Spain===
{{see also|Portugal–Spain football rivalry}}
The teams had faced each other in 41 previous matches including at the FIFA World Cup on two previous occasions: their first meeting was a [[2010 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Spain vs Portugal|1–0 round of 16 win]] for Spain at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] and then a [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group B#Portugal vs Spain|3–3 group stage draw]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]. Their latest match was the [[2025 UEFA Nations League final]] in which Portugal won 5–3 on penalties following a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/portugal/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Spain/|title=Portugal national football team: record v Spain|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 2, 2026}}</ref>

In the third minute, [[Mikel Oyarzabal]] dragged a shot from the left wide of the right post. In the 41st minute [[Nuno Mendes (footballer, born 2002)|Nuno Mendes]] hit the crossbar for Portugal after his shot deflected off [[Pedro Porro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/06/portugal-spain-world-cup-last-16-match-report|title= Merino strikes at the death for Spain to send Portugal and Ronaldo limping out|date=6 July 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>
In the 91st minute substitute [[Mikel Merino]] received a pass from fellow ‌substitute [[Ferran Torres]] on the left of the penalty area before shooting low left-footed to the left corner of the net for the only goal of the match. Portugal's defeat ended [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]'s World Cup career after he had confirmed earlier that this tournament would be his last.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cze9xg6480gt|title= Portugal 0 Spain 1|date=6 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>

Following the result, Portugal coach [[Roberto Martínez]] announced his resignation with immediate effect.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Beattie |first=Darren |date=6 July 2026 |title=Roberto Martinez to leave Portugal job following 2026 FIFA World Cup exit to Spain – 'Does not make sense to continue' |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/football/world-cup/2026/roberto-martinez-leaves-portugal-spain-defeat-last-16-cristiano-ronaldo_sto23317045/story.shtml |work=[[TNT Sports]]}}</ref> Meanwhile, Portugal striker [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] confirmed that this was his last World Cup match ahead of his expected retirement.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 July 2026 |title=Record-setting Ronaldo says goodbye to the World Cup |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/cristiano-ronaldo-farewell |website=[[FIFA]]}}</ref>

===United States vs Belgium===
[[File:Charles De Ketelaere Matt Freese Belgium v USA 6 July 2026-175.jpg|thumb|right|[[Matt Freese]] committing an error that led to Belgium's third goal by [[Hans Vanaken]] during the match.]]
{{See also|2026 Trump–FIFA red card controversy}}
The teams had previously faced each other seven times, most recently on March 28, a 5–2 win for Belgium in a friendly. They had also met twice in the FIFA World Cup: a [[1930 FIFA World Cup Group 4#United States vs Belgium|3–0 group stage win]] for the United States at the [[1930 FIFA World Cup|first World Cup]] (their only win ever against Belgium) and a [[2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Belgium vs United States|2–1 round of 16 win]] for Belgium in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/usa/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Belgium/|title=United States national football team: record v Belgium|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 2, 2026}}</ref> <noinclude>The [[2026 Trump–FIFA red card controversy|reversal of the suspension]] for [[Folarin Balogun]], who received a red card in his previous match against Bosnia and Herzegovina, has drawn condemnation of political manipulation from [[UEFA]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/02a7-2109c8e9ef81-de5a993db109-1000--uefa-statement-on-the-balogun-case/|title=UEFA statement on the Balogun case|date=July 6, 2026|website=UEFA.com}}</ref> and the [[Royal Belgian Football Association]], whose appeal was overturned.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/05/trump-fifa-balogun-world-cup-red-card-suspension.html|title=Balogun to start for U.S. vs. Belgium after Trump defends call to FIFA|first1=Garrett|last1=Downs|first2=Jack|last2=Sommers|first3=Dan|last3=Mangan|date=July 5, 2026|website=CNBC}}</ref></noinclude>

In the 9th minute, Belgium took the lead when [[Charles De Ketelaere]] side-footed low to the net from three yards out after a low cross from the left by [[Nicolas Raskin]]. The score was 1–1 in the 31st minute when a long-range free kick from [[Malik Tillman]] deflected off [[Hans Vanaken]] past [[Thibaut Courtois]] and into the net. Two minutes later, Belgium went back in front when De Ketelaere got his second goal by heading in at the back post to the right of the net after a cross from the left by [[Leandro Trossard]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/06/usa-belgium-world-cup-2026-match-report|title= Ragged USA crash out of World Cup with last-16 defeat to Belgium|date=7 July 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=13 October 2026}}</ref>
 
In the 57th minute, [[Hans Vanaken]] made it 3–1 when he shot low to the right of the net from outside the penalty area after an error in possession by US goalkeeper [[Matt Freese]]. [[Romelu Lukaku]] got a fourth goal for Belgium in the third minute of added time when he cut in from the left before scoring with a low shot to the right corner from inside the penalty area.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c24y8ded80vt|title= United States 1 Belgium 4|date=7 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=13 October 2026}}</ref>

The United States was the final co-host to be eliminated after Canada fell to Morocco and Mexico lost to England, with all three exits occurring in the Round of 16. Folarin Balogun's participation proved insignificant, as he and the rest of the U.S. team struggled for most of the match while Belgium easily breached the host team's defense.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tobin |first=Sam |title=Belgium end US World Cup dreams with 4–1 rout amid Balogun row |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/de-ketelaere-double-puts-belgium-into-world-cup-last-eight-ends-home-interest-2026-07-07/ |website=Reuters}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last4=Yomtov |first1=Seth |last1=Vertelney |first2=Nancy |last2=Armour |first3=Jordan |last3=Mendoza |first4=Jesse |title=USA eliminated from World Cup with nightmare moment in loss to Belgium |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/07/06/usa-belgium-world-cup-live-score-usmnt-lineups-watch-highlights/90817355007/ |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first=Ronald |last=Blum |date=2026-07-06 |title=Belgium beats US 4–1 to reach World Cup quarterfinals, taking advantage of defensive lapses |url=https://apnews.com/article/world-cup-united-states-belgium-score-0325e8102be7a88e852079deffd70ca0 |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

The United States registered its largest margin of defeat in a World Cup match since a 3–0 loss to the Czech Republic in [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]], and its worst goals-against performance in a World Cup match since a 5–1 defeat to Czechoslovakia in [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gray |first=Ben |title=Stats show the USMNT's loss to Belgium was their worst World Cup performance in decades |url= https://fansided.com/soccer/stats-show-the-usmnt-loss-to-belgium-worst-world-cup-performance-in-decades |website=Fansided.com|date= July 7, 2026}}</ref>

===Argentina vs Egypt===
[[File:Mostafa Shobeir Lionel Messi Argentina v Egypt 7 July 2026-167.jpg|thumb|right|[[Mostafa Shobeir]] saving the [[Lionel Messi]] penalty during the match.]]
Argentina had faced Egypt twice previously, a [[Football at the 1928 Summer Olympics#Semi-finals|6–0 victory]] in the semifinals of the [[1928 Summer Olympics]], and a 2–0 friendly win in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/argentina/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Egypt/|title=Argentina national football team: record v Egypt|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/argentina-v-egypt-06-june-1928-223814/|title=Argentina v Egypt, 06 June 1928|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 4, 2026}}</ref>

In the 15th minute Egypt went in front when [[Yasser Ibrahim]] headed into the right corner of the net from six yards out after a cross from the right by [[Marwan Attia]]. Six minutes later, Argentina was awarded a penalty when [[Haissem Hassan]] tripped [[Nicolás Tagliafico]] on the right of the penalty area. [[Lionel Messi]] took the penalty, which was saved by Egyptian goalkeeper [[Mostafa Shobeir]] down low to his left.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/argentina-vs-egypt/549861|title=World Cup 2026: Argentina 3–2 Egypt – Lionel Messi and holders come from two down as Enzo Fernandez wins classic|date=7 July 2026|work=Sky Sports|accessdate=10 July 2026}}</ref>

A second goal for Egypt, scored by [[Mostafa Ziko]] in the 60th minute after a counter-attack was ruled out after a VAR review brought it back for a foul on [[Lisandro Martínez]] at the start of the move. In the 67th minute Ziko made it 2–0 when he finished from six yards out after a low cross from [[Haissem Hassan]] from the right.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49298199/argentina-lionel-messi-world-cup-round-16-egypt-var-mohamed-salah|title=Messi, Argentina ride VAR drama to complete epic comeback vs. Egypt|date=7 July 2026|work=ESPN|accessdate=10 July 2026}}</ref>

In the 79th minute Argentina pulled a goal back when [[Cristian Romero]] headed powerfully to the right of the net from six yards out after a cross from the right from Messi. In the 83rd minute, Messi made it 2–2 when he half-volleyed the ball high in off the underside of the crossbar from twelve yards out on the right of the penalty area. In the 93rd minute, Argentina broke and [[Lautaro Martínez]] crossed from the right for [[Enzo Fernández]] to head into the right corner of the net from seven yards out to win the game 3–2 for Argentina. The winning goal was the 3,000th goal in tournament history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cdr4m2122lgt|title=Argentina 3 Egypt 2|date=7 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=10 July 2026}}</ref>

===Switzerland vs Colombia===
The teams had met four times prior, including Colombia's [[1994 FIFA World Cup Group A#Switzerland vs Colombia|2–0 group stage victory]] at the [[1994 FIFA World Cup]]. Their most recent meeting was also won by Colombia, a 3–1 friendly in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/switzerland/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Colombia/|title=Switzerland national football team: record v Colombia|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref> 

With this game, Colombia became the only team in the 2026 World Cup to play matches in all three host countries—Canada, Mexico, and the United States.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ramírez |first=Frida |date=6 July 2026 |title=Colombia will make history at the 2026 World Cup: it will be the only national team to have played in the United States, Mexico, and Canada |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/fifa-world-cup-2026/articles/colombia-will-make-history-at-the-2026-world-cup-it-will-be-the-only-national-team-to-have-played-in-the-united-states-mexico-and-canada-2026-07-06 |access-date=7 July 2026 |work=[[beIN Sports]]}}</ref> 

The game finished 0–0 after extra time and went to a [[List of FIFA World Cup penalty shoot-outs|penalty shoot-out]]. Colombia's [[Davinson Sánchez]] missed his penalty when he hit the underside of the bar with the ball bouncing back out, Switzerland's [[Manuel Akanji]] also missed when he kicked high over the bar. Switzerland goalkeeper [[Gregor Kobel]] saved down to his right from [[Cucho Hernández]], with [[Rubén Vargas]] scoring the winning penalty with a shot low to the left, sending the goalkeeper the wrong way.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/08/switzerland-colombia-world-cup-2026-last-16-match-report|title=Switzerland knock out Colombia on penalties to reach World Cup quarter-finals|date=7 July 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=8 July 2026}}</ref>

Switzerland reached the quarterfinals for the fourth time (after [[1934 FIFA World Cup|1934]], [[1938 FIFA World Cup|1938]], and [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]), their first in 72 years (since [[Austria v Switzerland (1954 FIFA World Cup)|1954]], when it hosted the tournament).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx2vrg8gzr1t|title= Switzerland 0 Colombia 0 (4–3 on pens)|date=7 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=8 July 2026}}</ref> Colombia's elimination from the tournament confirmed that Argentina became the sole representative from the [[Americas]] to proceed to the quarterfinals following their win against Egypt.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/fifa-world-cup-2026/articles/america-disappoints-at-the-2026-world-cup-only-argentina-survives-as-the-rest-of-the-continent-suffers-a-historic-failure-2026-07-07|last=Ramírez|first=Frida Samantha |title=America disappoints at the 2026 World Cup: only Argentina survives as the rest of the continent suffers a historic failure|date= July 7, 2026|website=[[beIN Sports]]}}</ref> 

This was the final game of the tournament played in Canada, as the remaining knockout matches—the quarterfinals, semifinals, third-place playoff, and final—were played entirely in the United States.

==Quarterfinals==

===France vs Morocco===
[[File:Ayyoub Bouaddi Michael Olise France v Morocco 9 July 2026-158.jpg|thumb|right|During the match between France and Morocco.]]
The two teams had met six times before, with France winning four matches. Their most recent meeting took place in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#France vs Morocco|semifinals of the last World Cup]], when France won 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/france/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Morocco/|title= France national football team: record v Morocco|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 4, 2026}}</ref>

In the 28th minute, France was awarded a penalty when [[Kylian Mbappé]] was fouled inside the penalty area on the left by [[Noussair Mazraoui]]. After a delay of over three minutes, Mbappé took the penalty and shot low to the right which was saved by Moroccan goalkeeper [[Yassine Bounou]].
[[Désiré Doué]] also had a low shot to the left from inside the penalty area saved by Bounou.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49319513/france-coach-deschamps-unhappy-wait-missed-mbappe-pen|title=France coach Deschamps unhappy with wait on missed Mbappé pen|date=9 July 2026|work=ESPN|accessdate=10 July 2026}}</ref>
In first-half stoppage time [[Lucas Digne]] hit a long range swerving shot from the left off the top of the crossbar and over.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/france-vs-morocco/report/549862|title=World Cup 2026: France 2–0 Morocco – Kylian Mbappe magic decides quarter-final after his own early penalty miss|date=9 July 2025|work=Sky Sport|accessdate=10 July 2026}}</ref>

In the 60th minute, France went in front when Mbappé received the ball from Doué on the left before curling a shot from just inside the penalty area into the top right corner of the net. It was his eighth goal of the World Cup. Six minutes later it was 2–0 when [[Ousmane Dembélé]] scored with a low shot from just outside the penalty area to the right corner which Bounou got a hand to but couldn't keep out.
Morocco was missing injured forward [[Ismael Saibari]] and failed to get a shot on target until the 84th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c30y244nl8mt#Report|title=France 2 Morocco 0|date=9 July 2025|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=10 July 2026}}</ref> As a result, this was the first time it failed to advance further in the knockout stage after its surprising success in [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]] where they finished fourth.

===Spain vs Belgium===
[[File:2026 FIFA World Cup Match 98, Spain v Belgium.jpg|thumb|[[SoFi Stadium]] during the match between Spain and Belgium.]]
The teams had previously met 23 times, including twice in the World Cup: a [[1986 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Spain vs Belgium|1–1 quarterfinal draw (Belgium won 5–4 on penalties)]] in [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]] and a [[1990 FIFA World Cup Group E#Belgium vs Spain|2–1 group stage win]] for Spain in [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]]. Their most recent meeting took place in 2016, when Spain won 2–0 in a friendly match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/spain/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/belgium/|title=Spain national football team: record v Belgium|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/belgium-v-spain-29-august-1920-223146/|title=Belgium v Spain, 29 August 1920|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 10, 2026}}</ref>

In the 30th minute, [[Fabián Ruiz]] gave Spain the lead when he finished right-footed to the net from six yards out after Belgian goalkeeper [[Thibaut Courtois]] had parried out a low shot from [[Dani Olmo]]. It was 1–1 in the 41st minute when [[Charles De Ketelaere]] headed powerfully to the left of the net from six yards out after a cross from the right by [[Timothy Castagne]], it was the first goal Spain had conceded in 649 minutes of World Cup football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/world-cup-2026/2026/0710/1582752-supersub-merino-strikes-again-as-spain-edge-out-belgium/|title= Supersub Mikel Merino strikes again as Spain edge out Belgium|date=10 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=8 October 2026}}</ref>

In the 71st minute Thibaut Courtois picked up a thigh injury and was replaced by [[Senne Lammens]]. In the 88th minute, Lammens spilled a long range shot from [[Pau Cubarsí]] with [[Mikel Merino]] getting to the ball first to finish to the net from six yards out to win the match for Spain. Merino had only been on the pitch for 117 seconds after replacing Dani Olmo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjwgg64ennqt|title=Spain 2 Belgium 1 |date=10 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=8 October 2026}}</ref>

This was the only match in the entire tournament where Spain conceded a goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/statistics/team-statistics}}</ref>

===Norway vs England===
The teams had previously faced each other 12 times, most recently in 2014, a 1–0 win for England in a friendly match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/norway/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/England/|title=Norway national football team: record v England|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 5, 2026}}</ref>

Norway went ahead after 36 minutes when [[Andreas Schjelderup|Andreas Schjelderup's]] left-footed strike from out on the left of the penalty area went over England goalkeeper [[Jordan Pickford]] and into the right corner of the net. England restored parity in first-half stoppage time when [[Jude Bellingham]] took a pass from Anthony Gordon and got into the left of the penalty area before shooting left-footed to the right of the net past Norway goalkeeper [[Ørjan Nyland]].<ref name="BBCNorwayEngland">{{Cite web |website=BBC Sport| last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=11 Jul 2026 |title=Norway 1–2 England: Jude Bellingham scores twice as Three Lions reach World Cup semi-final – BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgl33l55100t}}</ref>

[[Declan Rice]], who had been struggling with illness and injury leading into the fixture, was substituted at halftime, as well as Noni Madueke, being replaced with [[Eberechi Eze]] and [[Bukayo Saka]].<ref name="BBCNorwayEngland"/>

In the second half, a goal by Norway midfielder [[Torbjørn Heggem]] was ruled out due to [[Erling Haaland]] fouling midfielder Elliot Anderson, and [[David Møller Wolfe|David Møller Wolfe's]] header struck the bar.<ref name="BBCNorwayEngland"/>

In extra time, Bellingham scored the second goal for England when Nyland parried a shot towards him from substitute Morgan Rogers, with Bellingham finishing low to the net form six yards out.<ref name="BBCNorwayEngland"/> The Norwegians claimed the ball struck one of the [[Spidercam]] wires in the build-up to Bellingham's equalizing goal, but [[Snickometer]] ruled there was no contact. Had the decision been made that the ball struck the wire, the goal would have been ruled out and play restarted with a dropped ball.<ref>{{Cite web |website=BBC Sport| last=Rajan |first=Adwaidh |date=12 July 2026 |title=Did ball hit spidercam before England goal? Snicko says not – Norway unsure |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cd95335dp10o}}</ref>

[[Jude Bellingham]]'s two goals meant this England team was the first in [[FIFA World Cup]] history to have two players score six or more goals in a tournament, with [[Harry Kane]] having reached six in the previous match against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]]. Also, Bellingham's six goals in the tournament, none of which were penalties, is the joint-most non-penalty goals by an England player in a major men's tournament, along with [[Gary Lineker]] in the [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986 edition of the tournament]].<ref>{{Cite web |website=England Football| last=Hunt |first=Holly |date=12 July 2026 |title=Norway 1–2 England stats: Three Lions match winning streak |url=https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2026/Jul/12/england-norway-post-match-stats-world-cup-quarter-final-20261207}}</ref>

===Argentina vs Switzerland===
[[File:Argentina v Switzerland.jpg|thumb|right|Pre-match ceremony between Argentina and Switzerland.]]
This was Switzerland's first World Cup quarterfinal since the [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954 edition of the tournament]].<ref name="ESPNArgSwit">{{Cite web |website=ESPN Sport|date=12 July 2026 |title=Argentina survive Switzerland scare to book semifinal with England |url=https://www.espn.com.au/football/report/_/gameId/760513}}</ref>

Argentina had never lost to Switzerland in their seven previous encounters, winning five of those matches. Their first meeting took place at the [[1966 FIFA World Cup]], when Argentina [[1966 FIFA World Cup Group 2#Argentina vs Switzerland|won 2–0 in the group stage]] and their latest match was also at the World Cup, a [[2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Argentina vs Switzerland|round of 16 1–0 win (after extra time)]] in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/argentina/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Switzerland//|title=Argentina national football team: record v Switzerland|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 7, 2026}}</ref>

[[Alexis Mac Allister]] opened the scoring for Argentina after 10 minutes when he scored with a header to the right corner of the net after a corner kick taken from [[Lionel Messi]] from the left. Half way through the second half, shortly after [[Dan Ndoye]] scored the equalizer for Switzerland when he finished low to the net from the left of the penalty area. In the 72nd minute, [[Leandro Paredes]] was shown a yellow card for a tackle on [[Breel Embolo]]–however, [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] revealed Embolo falling before Paredes made any contact. Since Embolo had already received a booking, he was sent off. It was the second time a yellow card had been overturned at the tournament due to the "mistaken identity" protocol.<ref name="ESPNArgSwit"/>

The match went into extra-time and Argentina went 2–1 in front in the 112th minute when [[Julián Alvarez]] scored with a right footed shot to the top right corner of the net from 25 yards out on the left. It was 3–1 in the 120th minute when [[Lautaro Martínez]] side-footed into the right corner of the net from twelve yards out after the ball broke to him in the penalty area from a counter-attack.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4gyj35k3n3t|title=Argentina 3 Switzerland 1|date=12 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=8 October 2026}}</ref>

The match ended [[Lionel Messi]]'s record run of scoring in nine consecutive [[FIFA World Cup]] matches, stretching back to the Round of 16 match against [[Australia men's national football team|Australia]] in [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]].<ref name="ESPNArgSwit"/>

==Semifinals==
This is the first time in tournament history that the top four teams in the [[FIFA Men's World Ranking]] (as of the first match of the tournament) have all qualified for the World Cup semifinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Top four in FIFA/Coca Cola World Ranking set for historic showdown |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/top-four-fifa-coca-cola-ranking-semi-final |publisher=FIFA |date=July 12, 2026 |access-date=July 14, 2026 |archive-date=July 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714175811/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/top-four-fifa-coca-cola-ranking-semi-final |url-status=live }}</ref>  It's also only the third time in tournament history in which all four semifinalists are previous champions (along with the [[1970 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|1970]] and [[1990 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|1990]] editions).

===France vs Spain===
{{see also|France–Spain football rivalry}}
[[File:Aymeric Laporte France v Spain 7.24.26-061.jpg|thumb|right|During the match between France and Spain.]]
France and Spain had faced each other in 38 previous matches since 1922, including the [[UEFA Euro 1984 final]] (when host France won 2–0) and a [[2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Spain vs France|3–1 round of 16 win]] for France at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]]. Their latest encounter in a major tournament was at the [[UEFA Euro 2024]] semifinals, won 2–1 by Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/france/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Spain/|title= France national football team: record v Spain|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 9, 2026}}</ref>

In the 22nd minute, Spain was awarded a penalty when [[Lucas Digne]] kicked [[Lamine Yamal]] with his swinging left leg when trying to clear the ball. [[Mikel Oyarzabal]] scored the penalty with a powerful shot to the right of the net to make it 1–0. In the 58th minute it was 2–0 when [[Pedro Porro]] played a one-two with [[Dani Olmo]] on the edge of the penalty area before a side-foot finish with his right foot to the right corner of the net from the right of the penalty area.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/france-spain-world-cup-semi-final-match-report|title=Spain reach World Cup final after Oyarzabal and Porro sink sorry France|date=14 July 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=16 July 2026}}</ref>
The game finished 2–0 and Spain progressed to its second World Cup final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj3gdp4d3nnt|title=France 0 Spain 2|date=14 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 July 2026}}</ref>

===England vs Argentina===
{{see also|Argentina–England football rivalry}}
The teams had faced each other in 14 previous matches since 1951, with five of those encounters taking place at the World Cup: a [[1962 FIFA World Cup Group 4#England vs Argentina|3–1 group stage win]] for England in [[1962 FIFA World Cup|1962]], a [[1966 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#England vs Argentina|1–0 quarterfinal win]] for England (as host) in [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966]], a [[Argentina v England (1986 FIFA World Cup)|2–1 quarterfinal win]] for Argentina in [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]] (a match famous for [[Diego Maradona]]'s [[The hand of God|"hand of God" goal]] and the "[[Goal of the Century]]"), a [[1998 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Argentina vs England|2–2 round of 16 draw (Argentina won 4–3 on penalties)]] in [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]], and a [[2002 FIFA World Cup Group F#Argentina vs England|1–0 group stage win]] for England in [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002]]. Their latest match took place in 2005, a 3–2 win for England in a friendly match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/england/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Argentina/|title=England national football team: record v Argentina|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref>

After a goalless first half, [[Anthony Gordon (footballer)|Anthony Gordon]] put England into the lead in the 55th minute when he finished to the left of the net with his right foot from six yards out after a low cross in by [[Morgan Rogers]] from the right. As England looked to hold on to its lead, it went more defensive and switched to a back five. Argentina created chances after that with [[Jordan Pickford]] saving down low on the line from a close-range header by [[Nicolás González (footballer, born 1998)|Nicolás González]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13562935/world-cup-2026-england-1-2-argentina-three-lions-suffer-semi-final-loss-after-stunning-late-turnaround-by-holders|title= World Cup 2026: England 1–2 Argentina – Three Lions suffer semi-final loss after stunning late turnaround by holders|date=15 July 2026|work=Sky Sports|accessdate=16 July 2026}}</ref>
[[Alexis Mac Allister]] then saw his diving header from close range strike the left-side post. In the 85th minute, [[Enzo Fernández]] received a pass from [[Lionel Messi]] just outside the penalty area before shooting right-footed to the left corner of the net to make it 1–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/15/england-argentina-world-cup-semi-final-match-report|title= Argentina's late double breaks England hearts in dramatic World Cup semi-final|date=15 July 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=16 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ce8l15903k8o|title= 'Passive' and 'crumbled' – did Tuchel's defensive tactics cost England|date=15 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 July 2026}}</ref>

In the 92nd minute, Mac Allister saw his low shot from the left hit the right hand post before coming back to Messi, who crossed from the right for [[Lautaro Martínez]] to head into the left corner from three yards out to give Argentina a 2–1 lead. Argentina saw out the remainder of the added time to advance to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup final|final]] against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] for the second consecutive time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c77yp11e4r6t?page=2|title= England 1 Argentina 2|date=15 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 July 2026}}</ref> England's defeat ended its hopes of reaching the final and extended its period without a championship to 15 consecutive tournament appearances since [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=16 July 2026 |title=Why England's loss to Argentina felt like most painful in 60 years of hurt |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cj365n05mgdo |access-date=16 July 2026 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> However, England progressed to the third-place playoff against [[France national football team|France]], marking its first appearance in the bronze-medal match since [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]].

England manager [[Thomas Tuchel]] was widely criticized after the match for going too defensive after England took a 1–0 lead with over 30 minutes remaining. Between England scoring and Martínez's winning goal, England had just 12% possession.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Olley |first=James |date=July 15, 2026 |title=Thomas Tuchel vows to stay as England boss, defends tactics vs. Argentina |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49371265/thomas-tuchel-england-argentina-tactics-2026-world-cup-future}}</ref> After the defeat, Tuchel remarked that he fully intended to stay on as England manager, and proceeded to blame the country's "football DNA" for its World Cup exit.<ref>{{Cite web |website=Fox Sports|date=17 July 2026 |title=Bombshell dressing room reveal after WC blunder as England coach blames 'weak DNA' |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/fifa-world-cup-2026-thomas-tuchel-blames-englands-football-dna-for-semifinal-loss-to-argentina-reports-players-stunned-by-tuchels-tactics-will-tuchel-be-sacked-as-england-manager/news-story/c832fa31e8dfa214b1d968431d46ac8e}}</ref>

After the match, some Argentine players displayed a banner that read ''"Las Malvinas son argentinas"'' ("[[Falkland Islands|The Falkland Islands]] are Argentinian"), in reference to the territory [[Falkland Islands sovereignty dispute|dispute between Argentina and the UK]], and later left it on the pitch, in apparent contravention of FIFA rules.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/15/malvinas-is-argentinian-world-cup-holders-celebrate-win-over-england-with-banner|title='Malvinas are Argentine': World Cup holders celebrate win over England with Falklands banner|access-date=16 July 2026|website=The Guardian}}</ref> FIFA's ''Stadium Code of Conduct'' prohibits banners and related paraphernalia that are of a political or discriminatory nature inside stadiums,<ref>{{Cite web |website=ABC News |date=16 July 2026 |title=World Cup quick hits: England boss Thomas Tuchel's tactics allow Lionel Messi to orchestrate Argentina win |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-07-16/world-cup-quick-hits-england-argentina-messi-tuchel/106920846}}</ref> and the British government immediately urged FIFA to investigate the incident.<ref name="BBCArgentinaEnglandBanner">{{Cite web |website=ESPN|date=17 July 2026 |title=UK urges FIFA investigation of Argentina over Falklands banner |url=https://www.espn.com.au/football/story/_/id/49375290/argentina-inappropriate-falklands-banner-england-world-cup-clash-minister}}</ref> In a statement after the game, FIFA said: "As is standard ==Match for third place==
France and England had faced each other in 32 previous matches since 1923, with three of those encounters taking place at the World Cup. The first two meetings took place at the group stage and were won by England: [[1966 FIFA World Cup Group 1#England vs France|2–0]] as host in [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966]] and [[1982 FIFA World Cup Group 4#England vs France|3–1]] in [[1982 FIFA World Cup|1982]]. Their third tournament match (which was also their most recent meeting in any type of competition) took place in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#England vs France|quarterfinals of the last World Cup]], when France won 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/france/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/England/|title=France national football team: record v England|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 14, 2026}}</ref> This was France's first appearance in such match since [[1986 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Match for third place|1986]]. As both were European teams, this was already set pre-match as the [[European nations at the FIFA World Cup#Overview|twelfth consecutive World Cup in which European teams finished third]], stretching back to [[1982 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Match for third place|1982]], when [[Poland national football team|Poland]] defeated France.

England manager [[Thomas Tuchel]] made seven changes to his starting lineup that lost to Argentina in the semifinal, and he was [[Booing|booed]] by some England fans before kickoff amid criticism of his tactics.<ref>{{Cite web |website=Opta Analyst| last=Carr |first=Harry |date=19 July 2026 |title=France 4–6 England Stats: Three Lions Secure Third Place After 10-Goal Thriller |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/france-vs-england-stats-world-cup-2026-bronze-final}}</ref>

England stormed to a four goal lead by halftime via an early long-range strike by [[Declan Rice]], a header by [[Ezri Konsa]], and a double by [[Bukayo Saka]]. This marked the first time France had trailed by four goals at half-time of any international match since April 1930.<ref name="BBC_France_England">{{Cite web |website=BBC Sport| last=Smith |first=Emma |date=18 July 2026 |title=England 6–4 France: Bukayo Saka nets hat-trick in thriller as Three Lions finish third |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cly5lj1nqdxt}}</ref>

France made four changes at halftime, and by the hydration break in the second half, England's lead was cut to just a single goal, with [[Kylian Mbappé]] scoring twice (and ending up winning his second consecutive [[FIFA World Cup Golden Boot]]), and [[Bradley Barcola]] striking from inside the penalty box. [[Michael Olise]] almost restored parity for France, but his strike went wide. [[Djed Spence]] was then fouled in the France penalty box, resulting in a penalty to England, which was converted by Saka.<ref name="ESPN_France_England">{{Cite web |website=ESPN Sport| last=Masters |first=Tom |date=19 July 2026 |title=France 4–6 England: Bukayo Saka scores hat trick as Thomas Tuchel's men win thriller to finish third |url=https://www.espn.com.au/football/story/_/id/49394700/england-6-france-4-world-cup-2026-result-score-recap-bukayo-saka-kylian-mbappe-jude-bellingham}}</ref> Deep into injury time, [[Ousmane Dembélé]] charged into the penalty box and scored France's final goal of the match. Moments later, with full time imminent, [[Jude Bellingham]] made a solo run to France's penalty box and netted England's sixth goal.<ref name="ESPN_France_England"/>

Saka became just the second England player in history to score a [[Hat-trick#Association football (soccer)|hat trick]] in a World Cup knockout match, after [[Geoff Hurst]] in the [[1966 FIFA World Cup final|1966 final]],<ref name="BBC_France_England"/> and the fourth Englishman overall after [[Gary Lineker]] in [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]] and Harry Kane in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]]. The only other player to score a hat trick against France in the World Cup is [[Pelé]] for Brazil in [[1958 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Brazil vs France|1958]].<ref name="EnglandFootball_ENGFRA">{{Cite web |website=England Football| last=Hargraves |first=Dan |date=19 July 2026 |title=France 4–6 England stats: Saka follows Three Lions legend |url=https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2026/Jul/18/france-v-england-world-cup-third-place-playoff-post-match-stats-20261807}}</ref>

Jude Bellingham's seven goals over the tournament is the highest ever goal tally by an England player at a World Cup or UEFA European Championship tournament.<ref name="EnglandFootball_ENGFRA"/> Declan Rice's opening goal was England's second earliest goal in a World Cup match behind only [[Bryan Robson]], who scored after 28 seconds (also against France) in [[1982 FIFA World Cup Group 4#England vs France|1982]],<ref name="EnglandFootball_ENGFRA"/> which was also the last time England ever defeated France in a major tournament.

This was the first World Cup match in which France conceded six goals, and the first time conceding six goals in any international match since 1960, where they lost 2–6 to Switzerland in a friendly game.<ref>{{Cite web |website=Tribuna| last=Zakutskaja |first=Lera |date=19 July 2026 |title=France concede six goals for first time since 1960 |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/2026-07-19-france-concede-six-goals-for-first-time-since-1960/}}</ref>

England's victory secured its best World Cup finish since winning the competition in [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966]] (after previous attempts in [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]] and [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]]),<ref name="BBC_France_England"/> and was only its second victory in the World Cup against a higher-ranked opponent in the [[FIFA Men's World Ranking|FIFA Rankings]], previously defeating Argentina [[2002 FIFA World Cup Group F#Argentina vs England|1–0 in 2002]].<ref name="EnglandFootball_ENGFRA"/>

This was the highest-scoring match of the tournament, with a total of ten goals, as well as the highest-scoring World Cup bronze final of all time, eclipsing France's 6–3 win in over West Germany in 1958. It featured the joint fifth–most goals of any World Cup match, level with [[1958 FIFA World Cup Group 2#France vs Paraguay|France's 7–3 win over Paraguay in 1958]], and the most of any game in the tournament since [[Hungary v El Salvador (1982 FIFA World Cup)|Hungary beat El Salvador 10–1]] at the [[1982 FIFA World Cup]].<ref name="BBC_France_England"/> It was also the third-highest-scoring knockout-stage game at any World Cup, beaten only by [[Brazil v Poland (1938 FIFA World Cup)|Brazil's 6–5 extra-time win over Poland]] in [[1938 FIFA World Cup|1938]] and [[Austria v Switzerland (1954 FIFA World Cup)|Austria beating Switzerland 7–5]] in [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]].

==Final==
{{main|2026 FIFA World Cup final}}

[[File:Spain World Cup Winners Argentina v Spain 19 July 2026-1.jpg|thumb|right|Spain lifting the [[FIFA World Cup Trophy]]]]
Spain and Argentina had faced each other in 14 previous matches since 1952, with an even record as both teams won six matches along with two draws. They only met once at the World Cup, when Argentina [[1966 FIFA World Cup Group 2#Argentina vs Spain|won 2–1]] in the group stage of the [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966 tournament]]. Their latest meeting took place in 2018, a 6–1 win for Spain in a friendly.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/spain/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Argentina/|title=Spain national football team: record v Argentina|website=11v11.com|access-date=July 14, 2026}}</ref> They were expected to meet at the [[2026 Finalissima]] on March 27 at [[Lusail Stadium]] in [[Lusail]], Qatar. However, the match was cancelled as a result of the [[2026 Iran war|ongoing Iran war]] and the inability to reach an agreement to move the match to another location.<ref name="Cancellation">{{Cite press release|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/02a3-2026c631d084-67fdd005037f-1000--2026-edition-of-finalissima-cancelled/|title=2026 edition of Finalissima cancelled|date=15 March 2026|publisher=UEFA}}</ref> 

Spain's victory made it the second European nation to win a World Cup held in the Americas following [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]], the second nation to win a World Cup co-hosted by multiple countries after [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] in [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002]] (held in South Korea and Japan), and the first ever to do so in North America, where the [[1994 FIFA World Cup final|previous tournament]] in [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] (also in the United States) was won by [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=García García |first=Sergio |date=19 July 2026 |title=North and South America remain a curse for European teams: This is the only country to win the World Cup in the Americas |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/world-cup/north-and-south-america-remain-a-curse-for-european-teams-this-is-the-only-country-to-win-the-world-cup-in-the-americas-f202607-n/ |work=[[Diario AS]] |publication-place=Madrid, Spain}}</ref>

On July 29, ten days after the final, FIFA opened disciplinary proceedings against the [[Argentine Football Association]] (AFA) and its players following several tournament incidents. These included post-match altercations with Spanish players after the final, as well as a potential breach of regulations regarding non-sporting demonstrations. The latter charge stemmed from an incident four days prior to the final, following Argentina's 2–1 semifinal victory over England, when players displayed a banner reading ''"Las Malvinas son Argentinas"'' ("[[Falkland Islands|The Falklands]] are Argentine") in reference to the territorial [[Falkland Islands sovereignty dispute|dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Botcherby |first=Elizabeth |date=29 July 2026 |title=Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp3rkwgy6y7o |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=29 July 2026 |title=World Cup 2026: FIFA opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over several potential breaches including Falklands banner |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12098/13568194/world-cup-2026-fifa-opens-disciplinary-proceedings-against-argentina-over-several-potential-breaches-including-falklands-banner |work=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref>
